questions.question: 'Mopin', a festival to drive away evil spirits, is celebrated in the state of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arunachal Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• Mopin a festival of the Galo tribe of Arunachal Pradesh is celebrated in April every year.

 
 
• The Mopin festival is an important festival of the Galong tribe of Arunachal Pradesh which is celebrated in the month of Lumi (April) every year.
 
• Mopin is thought to bring wealth and prosperity to households and to the Gallon community as a whole. It is also believed that the festival drives away evil shadows and spreads God’s blessing of universal happiness.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Doljatra, also known as Dolyatra is a regional public holiday in the Indian state of West Bengal.

 
 
• It may also be known as Dol Purnima in Assam and Odisha.
 
• It is celebrated on the same day as Holi, the last full moon in the Hindu calendar, and also has the moniker 'Festival of Colours'.
 
 
 
• Ali-Aye-Ligang is a spring festival associated with agriculture, especially with the beginning of the Ahu paddy cultivation.
 
 
• It is celebrated by the Missing or Mishing an indigenous tribe of Assam, India.
 
• The festival marks the onset of sowing seeds.
 
 
 
• Me-Dam-Me-Phi is the most important Ancestor worship communal festival in the Ahom religion celebrated by the Ahom people on 31 January every year in memory of the departed.

questions.question: Drukpa Tsechi, a festival celebrated in Sikkim, is associated with which of the following personalities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Buddha.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **According to the English Calendar, **it falls somewhere around **July or August each year in Sikkim**. Coming to the legend behind the festival,** it is observed to celebrate Lord Buddha and his first preaching of the Four Noble Truths.**
 
• Drukpa Tsheshi is celebrated on the 4th day (Tsheshi) of the 6th month (Drukpa) of the Tibetan Calendar in Sikkim.
 
• This preaching was granted to his five disciples at the Deer Park in Sarnath.
 
 
• The** first noble truth acquaints with suffering.**
 
• The second noble** truth acclaims the truth of the origin of the suffering, accident, chance, illusion, and their causes.**
 
• The** third noble truth confirms the termination of suffering or the realization of 'Nirvana'.**
 
• The** fourth noble truth says about the truth of the Eight Fold Path, which eventually leads to Nirvana.​**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
 

 **Festivals**
 **Associated with personality**
 
 

 
 
 
• **Mahavir Jayanti **is one of the most significant festivals among the Jain community and is celebrated with splendour in India and across the world. **The festival commemorates the birth of Lord Mahavira.**
 
 
 **Lord Mahavira**
 
 

 
 
 
• Hindus across the world are celebrating **Diwali,** to mark the** return of Lord Rama to his kingdom Ayodhya with his wife Sita and his brother Lakshmana **after defeating Ravana in Lanka and serving 14 years of exile. The festival celebrates the victory of light over darkness. 
 
 
 **Lord Rama**
 
 

 
 
 
• **Janmashtami** is a Hindu festival celebrating** the birth of the god Krishna **on the eighth (Ashtami) day of the dark fortnight of the month of Bhadrapada (August–September)
 
 
 **Lord Krishna**

questions.question: 'Kamsale' is a dance form traditional to the states of_____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karnataka.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Kamsale of Karnataka, also known as Beesu Kamsale is a vigorous dance form of the Kannad-speaking inhabitants of the state that employs a great blend of aesthetic sublimity and martial dexterity.
 
• Karnataka's Kamsale is mainly practised in the districts of Mysore, Nanjagud, Kollegal and Bangalore.
 
• The religious aspect of Kamsale is prominent.
 
• It narrates the glory of Lord Mahadeswara Shiva and the performers are vowed a lifelong allegiance to the god.
 
• The art is transmitted orally and through closely guarded traditions transmitted from the preceptor to the pupil.
 
• ​Kamsale derives its name from the musical instrument used in the performance.
 
• Usually, Kamsale is performed by a group of three to five dancers, although the number can go up to twelve with singers included.
 
• They wear traditional dresses in gold and red.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Other Folk Dances of Karnataka are:-

 
 
• Krishna Parijatha,
 
• Bhootha Aradhane,
 
• Nagamandala,
 
• Karaga,
 
• Gaarudi Gombe,
 
• Joodu Haligi,
 
• Kamsale Nritya.

questions.question: Of the languages recognised as Classical Languages by the Government of India, as on 30th June 2020, which of the following is the latest?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odia.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

__
 
• Presently there are Six classical languages in India.
 
• Classical Languages are declared by the Government of India.
 
• Classical languages are declared following the guidelines of the Ministry of culture.
 
• The six classical languages and when they are declared
 
 
• Tamil in 2004,
 
• Sanskrit in 2005,
 
• Kannada in 2008,
 
• Telugu in 2008,
 
• Malayalam in 2013, and
 
• Odia in 2014
 
 
 
• All the Classical Languages are listed in the** Eighth Schedule of the Constitution.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Guidelines for declaring classical languages are

 
 
• High antiquity of its early texts/recorded history over a period of 1500-2000 years,
 
• A body of ancient literature/texts, which is considered a valuable heritage by generations of speakers,
 
• The literary tradition be original and not borrowed from another speech community,
 
• The classical language and literature being distinct from modern, there may also be a discontinuity between the classical language and its later forms or its offshoots.

questions.question: Chakradhar Samaroh is organized by the Ustad Allaudin Khan Sangeet Academy and the Chakradhar Lalit Kala Kendra to commemorate the glorious memory of Maharaja Chakradhar Singh who founded the________ Gharana in music.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Raigarh__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chakradhar Samaroh **is organized by the** Ustad Allaudin Khan Sangeet Academy and the Chakradhar Lalit Kala Kendra every year on Ganesh Chaturthi in Raigarh(Chattisgarh).**
 
• **Raja Chakradhar ****the **king of Raigarh found the Raigarh Gharana of music by combining different art forms.
 
• He belonged to the **Gond dynasty** who ruled Raigarh a princely state (currently in Chattisgarh) from **(1924 to 1947).**
 
• Previously it was organized by Gond rulers but after independence, it became halted but **restarted again in 1984 by

 Sarvodaya Leader Keyur Bhushan**.
 
• It was under his chairmanship that the** "Shri Chakradhar Lalit Kala Kendra"** was established.**​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• He was a **great patron of Indian art and music**.
 
• He used to invite and make perform musicians, dancers, and other classical artists in his court.
 
• In 1938, Chakradhar Singh headed the **first All India Music Conference held at Allahabad.**
 
• **Raigarh Gharana of Kathak** was formed under his rule.

questions.question: Which of the following states annually celebrates the 'Shirui Lily Festival'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Manipur__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Shirui Lily Festival**

 
 
• **​**It is a four-day fest featuring dance, food, music, traditional games and much fanfare celebrated in **Manipur** annually.
 
• **First celebrated** in the year **2017**.
 
• The main aims of the festival are to **increase awareness regarding the Shirui Lily plant and develop sustainable and responsible tourism in Manipur.**
 
• The festival is organised by the Department of Tourism, Manipur during the **peak blooming season of Shirui Lily**.**​**​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Shirui Lily:

 
 
• It is a unique species of ground lily that is found only in Manipur and cannot be transplanted anywhere else in the world.
 
• Botanical name - Lilium Mackliniae.
 
• It was declared the state flower of Manipur in 1989.
 
• It is considered endangered due to intense tourist activities and invasion of an invasive bamboo species.
 
• It was discovered by English botanist Frank Kingdon-Ward.

questions.question: Which of the following dance forms is derived from martial arts practices?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Chhau.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chhau is a semi-classical Indian dance that incorporates martial arts steps and techniques along with dance.**
 
• The dance form is known to originate in the states of Odisha, West Bengal, and Jharkhand.
 
• Chhau dance is a traditional dance form performed by men from Eastern India that enacts episodes from epics including Ramayana and Mahabharata.
 
• The main objective of this dance form is to celebrate martial arts.
 
• Chhau dance can be classified into three divisions based on the place it is performed; Mayurbhanj Chau of Odisha, Seraikella Chau of Jharkhand, and Purulia Chau of Bengal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jhora:**

 
 
• Jhora dance belongs to the state of Uttarakhand.
 
• It originated in the Kumaon region.
 
• This magical folk dance form binds people of all castes. Everyone enjoys the dance with a peaceful mind.
 
• Jhora dance is usually seen in the evening at weddings or fairs.
 
• As the dancers perform, everyone watching fills up with energy.
 
• Everyone jumps up to join the dance. It is generally performed in the spring season.
 
• People from all around the country come to witness this magnificent folk dance form.
 
• Jhora dance is incomplete without the famous traditional drum known as "Hurka".
 
• Imagine the drum beating in the background and a large group of people dancing their feet on the beats.
 
• The beats are different from traditional Indian drums.
 
 
 
• **Bharatnatyam** :
 
 
• It is the traditional dance of the state of Tamil Nadu.
 
 
 
• **Ghoomar:**
 
 
• It is a traditional folk dance of Rajasthan, India, and Sindh, Pakistan.
 
• The dance is chiefly performed by veiled women who wear flowing dresses called Ghaghara.
 
• The dance typically involves performers pirouetting while moving in and out of a wide circle.
 
• The word ghoomna describes the twirling movement of the dancers and is the basis of the word Ghoomar.
 
• Ghoomar is often performed on special occasions, such as at weddings and during Holi, and sometimes lasts for hours.

questions.question: ‘Lohri’, a festival of Punjab, is celebrated in the month of ______ every year.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __January__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Lohri, the bonfire festival of Punjab celebrated in the month of Magh, is symbolic of new beginnings.
 
• The festival is celebrated every year on January 13 with much enthusiasm and zeal.
 
• It is primarily the harvest festival of the Punjabis.
 
• This festival denotes the harvesting of the Rabi crops and hence all the farmers get together in order to thank god for giving them such a wonderful harvest.
 
• The rituals related to Lohri symbolize the attachment of the people with Mother Nature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Hola Mohalla, also called Holi, is a three-day long Sikh festival which normally falls in March.
 
• Maghi is the regional name of the Hindu festival of Makar Sankranti celebrated in Punjab and Himachal Pradesh.
 
• The Muktsar fair is one of the largest Sikh fairs held in Muktsar Sahib.

 
• Baisakhi festivals of Punjab is traditionally associated with the harvest of rabi crops.
